newsitem.title: USA: Exxon says completed Qatar gas plant study.
newsitem.headline: Exxon says completed Qatar gas plant study.

text.p: Exxon Corp said Wednesday that it has completed a feasibility study for a plant to convert Qatari natural gas to "synthetic" oil, a project that has been under discussion for several years.

"The Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC) and Exxon Al Khalij, an affiliate of Exxon Corp, have completed a study of the feasibility of applying Exxon's proprietary gas-to-liquids conversion technology to the development of the offshore Qatar North Field," Exxon said in a statement.

"The study results are currently being evaluated by the two companies to determine the potential role of gas-to-liquids conversion in the commercialization of Qatar's gas resources," the statement added.
QGPC and Exxon agreed in March, 1995 to undertake the study into converting the methane-rich natural gas in Qatar's giant North Field into crude and other liquids.
An Exxon official declined to give details of the feasibility study's findings.

However, Exxon Co. International's Africa, Middle East & Latin America regional manager J.M. Temple said at a conference in the United Arab Emirates earlier this month that Exxon's technology "is a major breakthrough...(with) economics comparable to LNG (liquefied natural gas) in many cases (and) economically attractive at current oil prices."

In a report last year by QGPC manager for downstream ventures, Ismail el-Emadi, he said: "The main product would be high-quality synthetic crude oil which is free of most of the impurities found in conventional crude oil, such as sulphur, nitrogen, nickel, vanadium, alphaltene, multi-ring aromatic and salt."
The technology has been existant for many years but generally not commercially viable unless crude oil prices were exceptionally high.
Many international oil concerns have been vying to exploit Qatari natural gas reserves, the third largest in the world after those and Russia and Iran.

One of Qatar's three multi-billion-dollar liquefied natural gas projects, a $6 billion project with Mobil Corp, Total SA of France, and Japan's Mitsui and Marubeni, is due to start shipping product to Japan in December.
QGPC's other two projects, with Mobil and Enron Corp, are projected to come on around the turn of the century.
Of Exxon's potential Qatari project, "there is less there than meets the eye," said a Washington-based Middle East consultant who didn't want to be named.

"If it works and Exxon gets it it would be a real breakthrough but (Qatar) is a tough place to do business right now," the consultant said. Cash-strapped Qatar will prioritize those projects which deliver quickest "and I don't see it happening for many years," he added.
